WIRELESS TELEGRAPHY (POSSESSION) RULES, 1933
WIRELESS
TELEGRAPHY (POSSESSION) RULES, 1933
Notification No. G.B.72-110,
dated 6th November 1983.-- In exercise of the powers conferred by Section
10 of the Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933, the Central Government is pleased to
make the following rules regarding the possession of wireless telegraphy
apparatus.
1. (i) These Rules may be
called the Wireless Telegraphy (Possession) under Rules, 1933.
(ii) They shall
come into force on the 1st January 1934.
2. In these rules, unless
there is anything repugnant in the subject or context:‑
(a) 'the Act'
means the Pakistan Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933.
(b) 'dealer'
means any person who deals in or manufactures for gain wireless telegraphy
apparatus defined in the Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933;
(c) 'complete wireless
set means' any apparatus which is capable in itself of transmitting or
receiving wireless signals with or without the addition of serials, valves,
power supply telephones, loud speakers or equivalent devicee; or
(d) the
Licensing Authority means the telegraph authority constituted under the
Telegraph Act, 1895, that is, the Director General of Posts and Telegraphs.
3. Subject to the
provisions of these Rules, every person other than a dealer is exempted from
the requirement of holding a licence to posses wireless telegraphy apparatus in
respect of--
(a) such
apparatus as is reasonably required for the purpose specified in current
licence issued to him under Section 4 of the Telegraph Act, 1885 to establish,
maintain and work a wireless telegraph; and
(b) wireless
telegraphy apparatus other than complete wireless sets.
(c) wireless
receiving apparatus established in any motor vehicle which is exempt from
registration in Pakistan; provided the said Wireless apparatus is not used for
the reception of wireless signals while in Pakistan.
3-A. Every person who has
or shall have applied to the Licensing Authority for a licence to Possess
wireless telegraphy apparatus shall up to and including the 28th February 1934,
the exempt from requirement of holding such licence.
4. Application for a
licence under these Rules shall he made in Form I and in accordance with the
instructions contained therein.
5. Licences shall he
issued to persons other than dealers in Form II and licences to dealers in Form
III.
6. Licences shall he valid
for period of twelve calendar months beginning from the first day of the month
of issue.
7. A fee of ten rupees shall be payable for
every licence issued under these rules.
8. Where the licensing
Authority is satisfied that a licence granted under these rules has been lost
or accidentally destroyed he may grant a duplicate, or substitute licence on
payment of a fee of two rupee's.
9. Licences issued under
these rules shall not he transferable.
10. No refund shall be
granted of any fees paid under these rules.
11. (1) Every person
licensed under these rules shall keep the wireless telegraphy apparatus
possessed by him at the premises specified in that behalf in the licence.
(2) A licence issued under these
rules shall ordinarily authorise the licensee to keep wireless telegraphy
apparatus in one building only; provided that the Licencing Authority may at
his discretion permit the licence to keep the apparatus in two or more
buildings.
(3) The Licensing authority may
during the currency of the licence after the specification of the permises
specified therein on receipt of a written application from the licensee
together with the licence for amendment.
12. Every dealer shall
require every person purchasing or acquiring a complete wireless set to produce
a valid licence issued in such person's name, Zither under these rules to
possess wireless telegraphy apparatus, or under the Telegraph Act, 1885 to
establish maintain and work a wireless telegraph:-
Provided that
this rule shall not apply--
(i) when the
person purchasing or acquiring a complete wireless set is not resident in
